caption:
In 1964 a textile-mill boss shaved an eighth of a dollar off a promised buyback. Warren Buffett was so annoyed he bought the whole failing mill, which he later called his dumbest stock ever and, by his own estimate, a $200 billion mistake. The twist: the mill's name became Berkshire Hathaway.

Sunday special. Get this week's five, free every Saturday → link in bio.

#WarrenBuffett #BerkshireHathaway #investing #stockmarket #history

Sources: CNBC (Oct 18 2010, Mar 2 2023), Fox Business, NPR Planet Money, AP (Sep 18 2026). Illustrated portrait. Not investment advice.

timeline.voice: A grudge cost Buffett $200 billion. You'd bite too.
timeline.caption: 12.5¢ grudge. $200B mistake.

timeline.voice: But it started with an eighth of a dollar.
timeline.caption: It started with 1/8 of a dollar.

timeline.voice: In 1962, he bought into a failing textile mill.
timeline.caption: A cheap mill, 1962.

timeline.voice: The boss agreed eleven fifty, then mailed less.
timeline.caption: Agreed: $11.50. Offered: $11.375.

timeline.voice: So he bought the mill and fired its boss.
timeline.caption: So he bought the whole mill.

timeline.voice: Decades later, he called it his dumbest stock ever.
timeline.caption: His dumbest stock ever.

timeline.voice: His own price tag: two hundred billion dollars.
timeline.caption: His own price tag.

timeline.voice: That money should have gone into insurance, he said.
timeline.caption: Why so much?

timeline.voice: The twist: that mill's name became a trillion-dollar company.
timeline.caption: The twist: $1T today.

timeline.voice: Pride is expensive. His lesson cost two hundred billion.
timeline.caption: The $200B lesson.
